comments.text: Two inverse screen-code digits copied into the status display; Mystery Maze file variants share number25.
Initial placement-stream pointer consumed by resident $7514/$4D0F before the private initialization callback.
Background and border color bytes. Loader uses pristine backup $3804/$3805 when publishing VIC colors.
Seven-byte bomb record pointer. The scanner searches for key $FF; target count $3013 need not equal record count. PLF13 uniquely omits the terminator after its four intended records.
Four pending callback pointers copied by $758A into $40C8-$40CF. A zero high byte leaves the existing no-op task; nonzero vectors are committed by the resident IRQ.
Initial player X low, X high and Y in hardware sprite coordinates, read by spawn $56E0. This is the start of each life, not multicolor drawing coordinates.
Initial target counter 12. Collection decrements it; special bomb callbacks can compensate the decrement or replace the table. Primary record list has 12 entries.
Resident perimeter-bullet slot limit 0; $6800 considers sprite slots1 through limit-minus-one. Private level actors can use other slots.
Ordinary collection adds this little-endian binary value (100) to the24-bit total score. Private callbacks may add an extra award first.
Initial little-endian bonus 1500. The resident countdown subtracts100 per256 enabled IRQ services; completion adds the remaining amount to total and bonus records.
Private initialization routine called after initial scenery drawing. Common no-op target is the RTS at $301F.
Main-thread entry selected by JMP($301B) at $759C; typically the spawn/collection/exit loop at $3050.
Private cleanup hook copied into the local JSR trampoline before completion or exhaustion. A target of $301F returns immediately.
Shared one-byte RTS used by empty initialization, cleanup and individual bomb callbacks in this overlay.
Eight ladder/up-rope X columns followed by six down-rope X columns, copied to $40B0-$40BD. Coordinates use160-wide multicolor space; $FF marks unavailable columns.
Two zero header bytes between the climb-column arrays and completion vector; the shared loader does not read them as part of those arrays.
Ordinary successful-level destination $5B00. The private loop calls cleanup before jumping through this word.
Exhausted-lives destination $5FFD, the resident jump to game-over presentation $6A80. This is separate from successful completion.
Two filename suffix characters '04'. Resident loader copies them into $40D3/$40D4; private cleanup can replace them before the next disk request.
Single $FF drawing-stream terminator, used as the no-change post-bomb action.
Zero byte after the empty drawing terminator and before collection-key coordinate offsets.
X/Y offsets applied by resident $55BF when reducing player position to the bomb lookup key. They adjust the coarse cell test, not the visible bomb positions.
Optional hook called before the matched bomb-record callback. A zero high byte suppresses the call; otherwise the resident patches JSR $5643 from this word.
Twenty loaded zero bytes align the private main loop to $3050. Header fields end at $303B; no private structure is assigned to this gap.

Spawn/reveal a life through $436A, then repeatedly check bomb collection through $436D. Zero remaining count at $3013 exits through success vector $3030 after setting divisor 9; death state $4028=2 waits for state 0, then respawns unless lives sentinel $40E4=$FF, which exits through $3032. Both exits call the header cleanup pointer. This variant also silences SID voice 3 when death state 2 is reached.

Patch local JSR operand from little-endian header $301D/$301E, invoke cleanup, return. In this file the header resolves to shared no-op RTS at $301F; the assembled $FFFF target is a placeholder, not a real call.

Drawing data $3094-$30FD read by Initial scenery $3094. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

12 seven-byte records [coarse key,x,y,callback low/high,post-draw low/high]. Terminator: $FF. Coordinates are160-wide bitmap positions. The resident scanner matches the key, calls both hooks, adds $3015 points, erases the bomb, follows the draw pointer and decrements $3013. This list is not bounded by the target counter.

Drawing data $3153-$318E read by Post-bomb drawing $3153, Post-bomb drawing $315D, Post-bomb drawing $3167, Post-bomb drawing $3171, Post-bomb drawing $317B, Post-bomb drawing $3185. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.
Fourth IRQ callback requests player death when phase $402B nonzero, collision shadow $4088 nonzero and current death state 0.
Eight compact 30-byte frames,240 authored bytes, expanded by $4376 into $8400-$85FF. Frames 10..13 animate falling objects;14..17 are the impact/explosion progression.
Expand graphics $31A4, set sprites 1..3 colour 2, clear their enabled states and frame pointers. They spawn later from the private IRQ callback.
Bits 02,04,08 for sprites 1..3; OR into $4059 when a hazard strikes the floor.
Complement masksFD,FB,F7 clear each hazard expansion bit on respawn.
Impact colour progression 1,7,2,6. Initial impact explicitly writes 1; subsequent phase indices 1..3 select 7,2,6.
Envelope 1B/00 then frequency 0C0C held 40 ticks, terminated 0. Queued with priority 6, release 0 and noise control $80.
Reserved index-zero byte, three explosion phase bytes for sprites 1..3, and saved actor index $32C5 used across RNG/sound calls.
Third callback loops sprites 1..3. Frame>=14 takes impact animation path; otherwise skip during death state 2 or zero $402C cadence. Disabled sprites attempt random spawn; enabled ones fall.

Only RNG byte<8 passes the initial 1-in 32 check, then a second byte must be 12..169. Set sprite X to twice that byte (24..338), Y0, frame 10, colour 2 and enabled 2; clear its expansion bit. Save X around shared RNG calls.
Advance Y3 per eligible callback; directly program SID voice 3 with pulse slide derived from negative Y, clear its scheduled priority $4040, and cycle frames 10..13. Y>=216 triggers impact.
Set colour 1, impact phase 1, frame 14 and expansion bit; play noise stream $32BA, shift X left 12 pixels to centre the expanded impact, then process the next hazard.

On odd $4020 ticks advance impact frame and colour phases 1..3. Phase 4 disables sprite, clears frame pointer and silences SID voice 3; then continue sprites through 3. This path runs independently of the ordinary falling cadence.
First seven bytes of unused loaded 00/FF fill after the final impact-animation RTS at $33F8. Completes the current page phase; no live callback or sprite source points here.
Four remaining pages of unused loaded 00/FF fill, including the page-boundary phase changes. All authored sprite frames and callbacks end before $33F9; no active pointer targets these pages.
